sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十八 列傳第二十二

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 28, Biography 22
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 28, Biography 22

sentences.zh: 裴邃字淵明，河東聞喜人，魏襄州刺史綽之後也。

translations.literal: Pei Sui, style name Yuanming, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong, a descendant of Pei Chuo, Regional Governor of Xiangzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui, styled Yuanming, came from Wenxi in Hedong and was a descendant of Pei Chuo, who had served as governor of Xiangzhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖壽孫，寓居壽陽，爲宋武帝前軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shousun lived as a resident in Shouyang and served as Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army under Emperor Wu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shousun had settled in Shouyang, where he served as chief clerk on the staff of Emperor Wu of Song's vanguard army.

sentences.zh: 父仲穆，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhongmu was General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongmu held the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 邃十歲能屬文，善《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At age ten Sui could compose literary works and excelled at the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Sui could already compose essays at ten and was accomplished in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 齊建武初，刺史蕭遙昌引爲府主簿。

translations.literal: In the early Jianwu era of Qi, the regional inspector Xiao Yaochang brought him in as chief clerk of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qi dynasty's Jianwu reign, Regional Inspector Xiao Yaochang recruited him as chief clerk of his headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 壽陽有八公山廟，遙昌爲立碑，使邃爲文，甚見稱賞。

translations.literal: At Bagongshan in Shouyang there was a shrine; Yaochang erected a stele for it and had Sui write the inscription, which won great praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaochang commissioned a stele for the shrine on Mount Bagong near Shouyang, he had Sui compose the inscription, which was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，對策高第，奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was recommended as an Outstanding Talent candidate, ranked at the top in the Palace Examination, and appointed Gentleman Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he scored highest on the imperial examination and was appointed Gentleman Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 東昏踐阼，始安王蕭遙光爲撫軍將軍、揚州刺史，引邃爲參軍。

translations.literal: When Dong Hun ascended the throne, Prince Shi'an Xiao Yao'guang served as General Who Pacifies the Army and Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, and brought Sui in as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Donghun took the throne, Prince Shi'an Xiao Yao'guang, who held the posts of general who pacifies the army and regional inspector of Yangzhou, recruited Sui as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 後遙光敗，邃還壽陽，值刺史裴叔業以壽陽降魏，豫州豪族皆被驅掠，邃遂隨衆北徙。

translations.literal: Later, when Yao'guang was defeated, Sui returned to Shouyang; it happened that the regional inspector Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei, the great clans of Yuzhou were all driven off and plundered, and Sui therefore moved north with the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao'guang was later defeated, Sui returned to Shouyang just as Regional Inspector Pei Shuye surrendered the city to Wei and the magnates of Yuzhou were driven away and plundered, so Sui went north with the others.

sentences.zh: 魏主宣武帝雅重之，以爲司徒屬，中書郎，魏郡太守。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Emperor Xuanwu held him in high esteem and appointed him to the Secretariat of the Minister of Education, as Director of the Secretariat, and as Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu of Wei valued him highly and appointed him to the secretariat of the minister of education, as director of the secretariat, and as administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏遣王肅鎮壽陽，邃固求隨肅，密圖南歸。

translations.literal: Wei sent Wang Su to garrison Shouyang; Sui firmly requested to follow Su and secretly plotted to return south.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei sent Wang Su to guard Shouyang, Sui insisted on accompanying him in order to plot his secret return to the south.

sentences.zh: 天監初，自拔還朝，除後軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian reign, he escaped on his own back to the court and was appointed Consultant of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianjian reign he made his own way back to the Liang court and was appointed consultant on the staff of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 邃求邊境自效，以爲輔國將軍、廬江太守。

translations.literal: Sui requested to prove himself on the frontier and was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sui asked to serve on the frontier and prove his worth, and was appointed general who assists the state and administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 時魏將呂頗率衆五萬奄來攻郡，邃率麾下拒破之，加右軍將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei general Lü Po led fifty thousand troops in a sudden attack on the commandery; Sui led his officers to repel and defeat them, and was promoted to General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei general Lü Po suddenly attacked the commandery with fifty thousand men, Sui led his troops to repulse and defeat them and was promoted to general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 五年，征邵陽洲，魏人爲長橋斷淮以濟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, during the campaign against Shaoyang Isle, the Wei forces built a long bridge across the Huai to secure their crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, during the campaign against Shaoyang Isle, the Wei army built a long bridge across the Huai to hold their crossing.

sentences.zh: 邃築壘逼橋，每戰輒克，於是密作沒突艦。

translations.literal: Sui built fortifications pressing against the bridge and won every battle; he therefore secretly constructed assault ships.
translations.idiomatic: Sui built fortifications to press against the bridge and won every engagement, and so secretly constructed assault ships.

sentences.zh: 會甚雨，淮水暴溢，邃乘艦徑造橋側，魏衆驚潰，邃乘勝追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When heavy rains caused the Huai to flood violently, Sui sailed his ships straight to the side of the bridge; the Wei army panicked and fled, and Sui pursued in victory and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains made the Huai flood; Sui sailed his fleet straight alongside the bridge. The Wei troops broke in panic, and he pursued them to a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 進克羊石城，斬城主元康。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Yangshi City and beheaded the garrison commander Yuan Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He next took Yangshi City and executed the garrison commander Yuan Kang.

sentences.zh: 又破霍丘城，斬城主甯永仁。

translations.literal: He also captured Huoqiu City and beheaded the garrison commander Ning Yongren.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Huoqiu and executed its commander Ning Yongren.

sentences.zh: 平小峴，攻合肥。

translations.literal: He pacified Xiao'an and attacked Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Xiao'an and laid siege to Hefei.

sentences.zh: 以功封夷陵縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiling with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiling with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Champion Army and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the champion army and administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 邃與鄉人共入魏武廟，因論帝王功業。

translations.literal: Sui went with fellow townspeople into the shrine of Emperor Wu of Wei and there discussed the achievements of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Sui entered the shrine of Emperor Wu of Wei with fellow townspeople and fell into discussion of the achievements of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 其妻甥王篆之密啓高祖，云「裴邃多大言，有不臣之迹。

translations.literal: His wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi secretly reported to the High Emperor, saying, "Pei Sui talks too boldly and shows signs of disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's nephew Wang Zhuanzhi secretly reported to Emperor Wu, saying, "Pei Sui talks too boldly and shows signs of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 」由是左遷爲始安太守。

translations.literal: " For this he was demoted to Administrator of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: " For this he was demoted to administrator of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 邃志欲立功邊陲，不願閑遠，乃致書於呂僧珍曰：「昔阮咸、顏延有『二始』之歎。

translations.literal: Sui aspired to distinguish himself on the frontier and did not wish to be idle in a distant post, so he wrote to Lü Sengzhen: "In the past Ruan Xian and Yan Yan sighed at being sent twice to posts beginning with shi [始].
translations.idiomatic: Sui wished to win distinction on the frontier and had no taste for a quiet, remote post, so he wrote to Lü Sengzhen: "In the past Ruan Xian and Yan Yan lamented the 'two shi'—being sent twice to posts whose names began with shi.

sentences.zh: 吾才不逮古人，今爲三始，非其願也，將如之何！

translations.literal: My talent does not match those ancients, yet now I suffer a third such 'shi' beginning—this is not what I wished; what am I to do!
translations.idiomatic: My talent falls short of theirs, yet now I face a third shi—this is not what I wanted. What am I to do!

sentences.zh: 」未及至郡，會魏攻宿預，詔邃拒焉。

translations.literal: " Before he reached the commandery, Wei attacked Suyu and he was ordered to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could reach his commandery, Wei attacked Suyu and he was ordered to resist them.

sentences.zh: 行次直瀆，魏衆退。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhidu on the march, the Wei army had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Zhidu on the march, the Wei army had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遷右軍諮議參軍、豫章王雲麾府司馬，率所領助守石頭。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Consultant of the Right Army and Marshal of the Cloud-Banner staff of Prince Yun of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help garrison Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: He was made consultant on the staff of the right army and marshal of the cloud-banner staff of Prince Yun of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help defend Stone City.

sentences.zh: 出爲竟陵太守，開置屯田，公私便之。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jingling, where he established military colonies that benefited both government and populace.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Jingling, where he established military colonies that benefited both the government and the people.

sentences.zh: 遷爲遊擊將軍、朱衣直閤，直殿省。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Strikes at Large Distances and Colonel of the Vermilion Robes and served in the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who strikes at large distances and colonel of the vermilion robes, serving in the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 尋遷假節、明威將軍、西戎校尉、北梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given Acting Credentials, made General of Illustrious Might, Western Rong Commandant, and concurrently Administrator of Northern Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted acting credentials, made general of illustrious might and western rong commandant, and concurrently administrator of Northern Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 復開創屯田數千頃，倉廩盈實，省息邊運，民吏獲安，乃相率餉絹千餘匹。

translations.literal: He again opened thousands of acres of military colonies; the granaries filled, frontier transport was spared, officials and people were at peace, and they jointly presented him with more than a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He again opened thousands of acres of military colonies; the granaries filled, frontier transport costs fell, officials and commoners lived in peace, and they together presented him with more than a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 邃從容曰：「汝等不應爾；

translations.literal: Sui said calmly, "You ought not to do this;
translations.idiomatic: Sui said calmly, "You should not do this;

sentences.zh: 吾又不可逆。

translations.literal: yet I cannot flatly refuse."
translations.idiomatic: yet I cannot simply refuse."

sentences.zh: 」納其絹二匹而已。

translations.literal: He accepted only two bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted only two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 還爲給事中、雲騎將軍、朱衣直閤將軍，遷大匠卿。

translations.literal: He returned as Gentlemen Attendant, General of the Cloud Cavalry, Colonel of the Vermilion Robes, and was transferred to Director of the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as gentleman attendant, general of the cloud cavalry, and colonel of the vermilion robes, and was transferred to director of the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，義州刺史文僧明以州叛入于魏，魏軍來援。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Putong era, the Administrator of Yi Province Wen Sengming rebelled with his province and went over to Wei, and Wei sent troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Putong era, Wen Sengming, administrator of Yi province, rebelled and surrendered his province to Wei, and Wei sent troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 以邃爲假節、信武將軍，督衆軍討焉。

translations.literal: Sui was given Acting Credentials and made General Who Gives Faith to Wu to supervise the armies in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was granted acting credentials and made general who gives faith to Wu to supervise the armies sent to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 邃深入魏境，從邊城道，出其不意。

translations.literal: Sui penetrated deep into Wei territory, taking the frontier road and striking where they did not expect him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui drove deep into Wei territory by the frontier road and took the enemy by surprise.

sentences.zh: 魏所署義州刺史封壽據檀公峴，邃擊破之，遂圍其城，壽麵縛請降，義州平。

translations.literal: Feng Shou, whom Wei had appointed Administrator of Yi Province, held Tanggong Pass; Sui defeated him, then besieged his city; Shou came out bound and asked to surrender, and Yi Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shou, whom Wei had appointed administrator of Yi province, held Tanggong Pass; Sui defeated him, besieged his city, and Shou came out with his face bound to surrender. Yi province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 除持節、督北徐州諸軍事、信武將軍、北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Northern Xuzhou, General Who Gives Faith to Wu, and Regional Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Northern Xuzhou, general who gives faith to Wu, and regional inspector of Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之職，又遷督豫州北豫霍三州諸軍事、豫州刺史，鎮合肥。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was again transferred to Supervisor of Military Affairs in Yuzhou, Northern Yuzhou, and Huo, made Regional Inspector of Yuzhou, and garrisoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up that post he was transferred to supervise military affairs in Yuzhou, Northern Yuzhou, and Huo, made regional inspector of Yuzhou, and stationed at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號宣毅將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his title was advanced to General Who Proclaims Martial Resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to general who proclaims martial resolve.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大軍將北伐，以邃督征討諸軍事，率騎三千，先襲壽陽。

translations.literal: That year, as the main army was about to march north, Sui was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for the punitive campaign, leading three thousand cavalry in a preliminary strike on Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as the main army prepared its northern campaign, Sui was put in charge of the punitive forces, leading three thousand cavalry in a preliminary strike on Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，夜至壽陽，攻其郛，斬關而入，一日戰九合，爲後軍蔡秀成失道不至，邃以援絕拔還。

translations.literal: On the day renxu of the ninth month he reached Shouyang by night, attacked the outer wall, cut through the gate and entered, and fought nine engagements in one day; the rear army under Cai Xiucheng lost its way and did not arrive, and Sui, his reinforcements cut off, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renxu of the ninth month he reached Shouyang by night, attacked the outer wall, cut through the gate and entered, and fought nine engagements in a single day; the rear army under Cai Xiucheng lost its way and never arrived, and with his reinforcements cut off Sui withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是邃復整兵，收集士卒，令諸將各以服色相別。

translations.literal: Sui then reorganized his troops, gathered his soldiers, and ordered each general to distinguish himself by the color of his uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Sui then reorganized his army, rallied his troops, and ordered each commander to wear a distinctive uniform color.

sentences.zh: 邃自爲黃袍騎，先攻狄丘、甓城、黎漿等城，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Sui himself rode in a yellow robe and led the attack on Diqiu, Picheng, Lijiang, and other cities, all of which he took.
translations.idiomatic: Sui himself rode at the head in a yellow robe and led the assault on Diqiu, Picheng, Lijiang, and other cities, all of which fell.

sentences.zh: 屠安成、馬頭、沙陵等戍。

translations.literal: He slaughtered the garrisons at Ancheng, Matou, Shaling, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed and destroyed the garrisons at Ancheng, Matou, Shaling, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 是冬，始修芍陂。

translations.literal: That winter he began repairing the Quepi Reservoir.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he began repairing the Quepi Reservoir.

sentences.zh: 明年，復破魏新蔡郡，略地至於鄭城，汝潁之間，所在回應。

translations.literal: The next year he again defeated Wei's Xincai commandery, carried his raids as far as Zheng City, and everywhere between the Ru and Ying rivers people rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again defeated Wei's Xincai commandery and carried his raids as far as Zheng City; throughout the region between the Ru and Ying rivers, people rose in response wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 魏壽陽守將長孫稚、河間王元琛率衆五萬，出城挑戰。

translations.literal: Changsun Zhi, the Wei garrison commander of Shouyang, and Prince Hejian Yuan Chen led fifty thousand troops out of the city to offer battle.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, Wei's garrison commander at Shouyang, and Prince Hejian Yuan Chen led fifty thousand men out of the city to offer battle.

sentences.zh: 邃勒諸將爲四甄以待之，令直閤將軍李祖憐偽遁以引稚，稚等悉衆追之，四甄競發，魏衆大敗。

translations.literal: Sui arrayed his generals in four formations to await them and ordered Colonel of the Palace Gateway Li Zuling to feign retreat and lure Zhi; Zhi and the others pursued with their entire force, the four formations closed in at once, and the Wei army suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sui drew up his commanders in four battle formations and ordered Colonel Li Zuling to feign retreat and lure Zhi forward; Zhi pursued with his entire force, the four formations closed in at once, and the Wei army was routed.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: They took more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand enemy heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 稚等奔走，閉門自固，不敢復出。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others fled, barred their gates, and dared not venture out again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the others fled back inside, barred the gates, and dared not venture out again.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，卒於軍中。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the fifth month, he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、左衛將軍，給鼓吹一部，進爵爲侯，增邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, granted one set of ceremonial music, raised to marquisate, and his fief increased by seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as palace attendant and general of the left guard, granted one set of ceremonial music, raised to marquis, and his fief increased by seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈。

translations.literal: His temple name was Lie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Lie.

sentences.zh: 邃少言笑，沉深有思略，爲政寬明，能得士心。

translations.literal: Sui spoke little and seldom smiled, was deep and possessed of strategic thought, administered affairs with generosity and clarity, and won the hearts of his officers.
translations.idiomatic: Sui spoke little and seldom smiled. Deep and resourceful, he governed with generosity and clarity and won the loyalty of his officers.

sentences.zh: 居身方正有威重，將吏憚之，少敢犯法。

translations.literal: In bearing he was upright and commanding, so that subordinates feared him and few dared break the law.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and imposing in person, he inspired such respect among his officers that few dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 及其卒也，淮、肥間莫不流涕，以爲邃不死，洛陽不足拔也。

translations.literal: At his death people between the Huai and Fei wept without exception, believing that had Sui lived, Luoyang would not have been hard to take.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people throughout the Huai and Fei region wept, believing that if Sui had lived, Luoyang would not have been hard to take.

sentences.zh: 子之禮

translations.literal: His son Zhi-li
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi-li

sentences.zh: 子之禮，字子義，自國子生推第，補邵陵王國左常侍、信威行參軍。

translations.literal: Zhi-li, style name Ziyi, advanced from the Imperial Academy by examination to serve as Left Attendant of the Prince of Shaoling and Acting Staff Officer of Trust and Might.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi-li, styled Ziyi, advanced from the Imperial Academy by examination and was appointed left attendant of the Prince of Shaoling and acting staff officer of trust and might.

sentences.zh: 王爲南兗，除長流參軍，未行，仍留宿衛，補直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When the prince was assigned to Southern Yanzhou, he was appointed Chief Registrar, but before he took up the post he remained on palace guard duty and was made Colonel of the Palace Gateway.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was assigned to Southern Yanzhou, Zhi-li was appointed chief registrar, but before he could take up the post he remained on palace guard duty and was made colonel of the palace gateway.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋襲封，因請隨軍討壽陽，除雲麾將軍，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning; when the mourning period ended he inherited the fief and asked to join the campaign against Shouyang, was made General of the Cloud Banner, then promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he inherited the fief and asked to join the campaign against Shouyang; he was made general of the cloud banner and then promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 又別攻魏廣陵城，平之，除信武將軍、西豫州刺史，加輕車將軍，除黃門侍郎，遷中軍宣城王司馬。

translations.literal: He separately attacked and pacified the Wei city of Guangling, was made General Who Gives Faith to Wu and Regional Inspector of Western Yu Province, with additional rank as General of Light Chariots, then Palace Gentleman, and transferred to Marshal of the Central Army under Prince Xuan of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He separately attacked and pacified the Wei city of Guangling, was made general who gives faith to Wu and regional inspector of Western Yu province, with the additional rank of general of light chariots, then palace gentleman, and transferred to marshal of the central army under Prince Xuan of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋爲都督北徐仁睢三州諸軍事、信武將軍、北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for Northern Xu, Ren, and Sui provinces, General Who Gives Faith to Wu, and Regional Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of military affairs for Northern Xu, Ren, and Sui provinces, general who gives faith to Wu, and regional inspector of Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵太子左衛率，兼衛尉卿，轉少府卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and concurrently Director of Court Propriety, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left commandant of the crown prince's guard and concurrently director of court propriety, then transferred to director of the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He died; his temple name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子政，承聖中，官至給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zheng, during the Chengsheng era, rose to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng, during the Chengsheng era, rose to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，隨例入西魏。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell he followed the usual practice of being taken into Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he was taken into Western Wei along with the others.

sentences.zh: 兄子之高

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Zhigao
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Zhigao

sentences.zh: 之高字如山，邃兄中散大夫髦之子也。

translations.literal: Zhigao, style name Rushan, was the son of Sui's elder brother Mao, who had been Palace Attendant in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao, styled Rushan, was the son of Sui's elder brother Mao, who had served as palace attendant in the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 起家州從事、新都令、奉朝請，遷參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as a provincial aide, Magistrate of Xindu, and Gentleman Attendant at Court, then was transferred to Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a provincial aide, magistrate of Xindu, and gentleman attendant at court, then was transferred to staff officer.

sentences.zh: 頗讀書，少負意氣，常隨叔父邃征討，所在立功，甚爲邃所器重，戎政咸以委焉。

translations.literal: He read widely, possessed a bold spirit in youth, and often accompanied his uncle Sui on campaign, distinguishing himself wherever he went; Sui valued him highly and entrusted him with all military and administrative matters.
translations.idiomatic: Well read and spirited in youth, he often accompanied his uncle Sui on campaign and distinguished himself wherever he went; Sui valued him highly and entrusted him with all military and administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 壽陽之役，邃卒於軍所，之高隸夏侯夔，平壽陽，仍除平北豫章長史、梁郡太守，封都城縣男，邑二百五十戶。

translations.literal: In the Shouyang campaign, when Sui died in camp, Zhigao served under Xiahou Kui in the conquest of Shouyang, then was appointed Chief Clerk of the North Pacification staff of Yuzhang and Administrator of Liang Commandery, and enfeoffed as Baron of Ducheng with a fief of two hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shouyang campaign, when Sui died in camp, Zhigao served under Xiahou Kui in the capture of Shouyang; he was then appointed chief clerk on the north-pacification staff of Yuzhang and administrator of Liang commandery, and enfeoffed as Baron of Ducheng with a fief of two hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 時魏汝陰來附，敕之高應接，仍除假節、飆勇將軍、潁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wei Yin of Runan came over to submit, he was ordered to receive him and was given Acting Credentials, made General of Swift Valor, and Administrator of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Runan in Wei submitted, Zhigao was ordered to receive the surrender and was granted acting credentials, made general of swift valor, and appointed regional inspector of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 士民夜反，逾城而入，之高率家僮與麾下奮擊，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: That night the gentry and commoners rebelled, climbing the walls to enter the city; Zhigao led his household retainers and personal troops in fierce resistance until the insurgents dispersed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night the local gentry and commoners rebelled and climbed over the walls into the city; Zhigao led his household retainers and personal troops in fierce resistance until the rebels scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 父憂還京。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 起爲光遠將軍，合討陰陵盜賊，平之，以爲譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was recalled as General of Expansive Light and joined in the joint campaign against the bandits of Yinling, pacified them, and was made Regional Inspector of Qiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as general of expansive light, he joined the joint campaign against the bandits of Yinling, pacified them, and was made regional inspector of Qiao province.

sentences.zh: 又還爲左軍將軍，出爲南譙太守、監北徐州，遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was again made General of the Left Army, went out as Administrator of Southern Qiao and Overseer of Northern Xu Province, then promoted to Outer Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made general of the left army, went out as administrator of Southern Qiao and overseer of Northern Xu province, then promoted to outer palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋除雄信將軍、西豫州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made General of Mighty Trust and Regional Inspector of Western Yu Province, with all other posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general of mighty trust and regional inspector of Western Yu province, with his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，之高率衆入援，南豫州刺史、鄱陽嗣王範命之高總督江右援軍諸軍事，頓于張公洲。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zhigao led his troops in relief; Prince Fan, Prince of Poyang and Regional Inspector of Southern Yu Province, ordered Zhigao to assume supreme command of the relief armies on the right bank of the Yangtze and encamped at Zhanggong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zhigao led his troops to the relief of the capital; Prince Fan of Poyang, regional inspector of Southern Yu province, ordered Zhigao to assume supreme command of the relief armies on the right bank of the Yangtze and encamped at Zhanggong Isle.

sentences.zh: 柳仲禮至橫江，之高遣船舸二百餘艘迎致仲禮，與韋粲等俱會青塘立營，據建興苑。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhongli arrived at Hengjiang, Zhigao sent more than two hundred boats to meet and escort him; together with Wei Can and others he established camp at Qingtang and occupied the Jianxing Park grounds.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhongli arrived at Hengjiang, Zhigao sent more than two hundred boats to meet him; together with Wei Can and others he established camp at Qingtang and occupied the grounds of Jianxing Park.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，之高還合肥，與鄱陽王範西上。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Zhigao returned to Hefei and went west with Prince Fan of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Zhigao returned to Hefei and marched west with Prince Fan of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 稍至新蔡，衆將一萬，未有所屬。

translations.literal: By degrees he reached Xincai with ten thousand troops and no clear superior to join.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually made his way to Xincai with ten thousand troops but had no clear superior to serve under.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣蕭慧正召之，以爲侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sent Xiao Huizheng to summon him; he was appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan sent Xiao Huizheng to summon him and appointed him palace attendant and general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 到江陵，承制除特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Jiangling he was appointed by imperial order as Special Grand Master and Grand Master of the Golden Registry with imperial carriage and purple seal.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Jiangling he was appointed by imperial order as special grand master and grand master of the golden registry with imperial carriage and purple seal.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、儀同三司，鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Commissioner Equal to the Three Excellencies, with one set of ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as palace attendant and commissioner equal to the three excellencies, with one set of ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His temple name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 子畿，累官太子右衛率、雋州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Ji held successive offices as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and Regional Inspector of Jun Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji held successive posts as right commandant of the crown prince's guard and regional inspector of Jun province.

sentences.zh: 西魏攻陷江陵，畿力戰死之。

translations.literal: When Western Wei captured Jiangling, Ji fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei captured Jiangling, Ji fought fiercely and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 之高弟之平

translations.literal: Zhigao's younger brother Zhiping
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao's younger brother Zhiping

sentences.zh: 之平字如原，之高第五弟。

translations.literal: Zhiping, style name Ruyuan, was Zhigao's fifth younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping, styled Ruyuan, was Zhigao's fifth younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少亦隨邃征討，以軍功封都亭侯。

translations.literal: In youth he too followed Sui on campaign and through military merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he too followed Sui on campaign and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting.

sentences.zh: 歷武陵王常侍、扶風、弘農二郡太守，不行，除譙州長史、陽平太守。

translations.literal: He held successive posts as Attendant to the Prince of Wuling and Administrator of Fufeng and Hongnong, but did not take office; he was appointed Chief Clerk of Qiao Province and Administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive appointments as attendant to the Prince of Wuling and as administrator of Fufeng and Hongnong, but did not take office; he was appointed chief clerk of Qiao province and administrator of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 拒侯景，城陷後，遷散騎常侍、右衛將軍、太子詹事。

translations.literal: After resisting Hou Jing, when the city fell he was transferred to Palace Attendant, General of the Right Guard, and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After resisting Hou Jing, when the city fell he was transferred to palace attendant, general of the right guard, and grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 之平弟之橫

translations.literal: Zhiping's younger brother Zhiheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping's younger brother Zhiheng

sentences.zh: 時尋陽王大心在江州，範副梅思立密要大心襲湓城，之橫斬思立而拒大心。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Xunyang Wang Daxin was in Jiangzhou; Fan's deputy Mei Silì secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng; Zhiheng beheaded Silì and resisted Daxin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Xunyang Wang Daxin held Jiangzhou; Mei Silì, a deputy of Prince Fan, secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng, but Zhiheng executed Silì and resisted Daxin.

sentences.zh: 大心以州降景。

translations.literal: Daxin surrendered the province to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Daxin surrendered his province to Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 之橫率衆與兄之高同歸元帝，承制除散騎常侍、廷尉卿，出爲河東內史。

translations.literal: Zhiheng led his troops and, together with his elder brother Zhigao, submitted to Emperor Yuan; by imperial order he was appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Court of Justice, then went out as Interior Minister of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiheng led his troops and, together with his elder brother Zhigao, submitted to Emperor Yuan, who appointed him palace attendant and director of the court of justice by imperial order, then sent him out as interior minister of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 又隨王僧辯拒侯景於巴陵，景退，遷持節、平北將軍、東徐州刺史，中護軍，封豫寧侯，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He again followed Wang Sengbian in resisting Hou Jing at Baling; when Jing withdrew, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Regional Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, made Central Protector of the Army, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuníng with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Wang Sengbian in resisting Hou Jing at Baling; when Jing withdrew, he was made bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the north, and regional inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, appointed central protector of the army, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuníng with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又隨僧辯追景，平郢、魯、江、晉等州，恒爲前鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: He again followed Sengbian in pursuing Jing, pacified Ying, Lu, Jiang, Jin, and other provinces, and was always in the vanguard breaking enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Sengbian in pursuing Jing and pacified Ying, Lu, Jiang, Jin, and other provinces, always serving in the vanguard to break enemy formations.

sentences.zh: 仍至石頭，破景，景東奔，僧辯令之橫與杜崱入守臺城。

translations.literal: He then reached Stone City, defeated Jing, and Jing fled east; Sengbian ordered Zhiheng and Du Kan to enter and garrison Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: He then reached Stone City, defeated Jing, and Jing fled east; Sengbian ordered Zhiheng and Du Kan to enter and garrison Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 及陸納據湘州叛，又隸王僧辯南討焉。

translations.literal: When Lu Na seized Xiangzhou in rebellion, he again served under Wang Sengbian in the southern punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Na seized Xiangzhou in rebellion, he again served under Wang Sengbian in the southern punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 于陣斬納將李賢明，遂平之。

translations.literal: In battle he beheaded Na's general Li Xianming and thus pacified the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he killed Na's general Li Xianming and thus pacified the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 又破武陵王於硤口。

translations.literal: He also defeated the Prince of Wuling at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the Prince of Wuling at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 還除吳興太守，乃作百幅被，以成其初志。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Administrator of Wuxing, and there he made a quilt of a hundred layers of cloth to fulfill his early wish.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed administrator of Wuxing, where he made a quilt of a hundred layers of cloth to fulfill an early wish of his.

sentences.zh: 後江陵陷，齊遣上黨王高渙挾貞陽侯攻東關，晉安王方智承制，以之橫爲使持節、鎮北將軍、徐州刺史，都督衆軍，給鼓吹一部，出守蘄城。

translations.literal: Later, when Jiangling fell, Qi sent Prince Shangdang Gao Huan, escorting the Marquis of Zhenyang, to attack Dongguan; Prince Jin'an Fangzhi, acting by imperial order, appointed Zhiheng Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the North, and Regional Inspector of Xuzhou, with supreme command of the armies, granted one set of ceremonial music, and sent him out to garrison Qicheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, Qi sent Prince Shangdang Gao Huan, escorting the Marquis of Zhenyang, to attack Dongguan; Prince Jin'an Fangzhi, acting by imperial order, appointed Zhiheng bearer of the staff, general who guards the north, and regional inspector of Xuzhou, with supreme command of the armies and one set of ceremonial music, and sent him out to garrison Qicheng.

sentences.zh: 之橫營壘未周，而齊軍大至，兵盡矢窮，遂於陣沒，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Before Zhiheng's fortifications were complete, the Qi army arrived in force; his troops were exhausted and his arrows spent, and he fell in battle at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhiheng's fortifications were complete, the Qi army arrived in force; his troops were exhausted and his arrows spent, and he fell in battle at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空公，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Duke of Works; his temple name was Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as palace attendant and duke of works; his posthumous name was Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 子鳳寶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fengbao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengbao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 夏侯亶

translations.literal: Xiahou Dan
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dan

sentences.zh: 夏侯亶字世龍，車騎將軍詳長子也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Dan, style name Shilong, was the eldest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Dan, styled Shilong, was the eldest son of General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiang.

sentences.zh: 齊初，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he began his career as Gentleman Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qi dynasty he began his career as gentleman attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 永元末，詳爲西中郎南康王司馬，隨府鎮荊州，亶留京師，爲東昏聽政主帥。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era, Xiang served as Marshal of the Western Central Commandery under the Prince of Nankang and followed the headquarters to garrison Jingzhou; Dan remained in the capital as chief commander for Donghun's audience with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongyuan era, Xiang served as marshal under the Prince of Nankang's western central commandery and followed the headquarters to garrison Jingzhou; Dan remained in the capital as chief commander for Emperor Donghun's audiences on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及崔慧景作亂，亶以捍禦功，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing rebelled, Dan was made General of Valiant Cavalry for his merit in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing rebelled, Dan was made general of valiant cavalry for his merit in defense.

sentences.zh: 及高祖起師，詳與長史蕭穎胄協同義舉，密遣信下都迎亶，亶乃齎宣德皇后令，令南康王纂承大統，封十郡爲宣城王，進位相國，置僚屬，選百官。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor raised his army, Xiang and Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou joined in the righteous uprising and secretly sent a messenger to the capital to summon Dan; Dan then carried the order of Empress Xuande, had the Prince of Nankang succeed to the great succession, enfeoffed ten commanderies as Prince of Xuancheng, advanced him to Chancellor of State, established a staff, and selected the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu raised his army, Xiang and Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou joined the righteous uprising and secretly sent a messenger to the capital to summon Dan; Dan then carried the order of Empress Xuande, had the Prince of Nankang succeed to the throne, enfeoffed ten commanderies to him as Prince of Xuancheng, advanced him to chancellor of state, established a staff, and selected the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，以亶爲尚書吏部郎，俄遷侍中，奉璽於高祖。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Dan was appointed Director of the Personnel Bureau in the Ministry of Works; soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and presented the imperial seal to the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified, Dan was appointed director of the personnel bureau in the ministry of works; soon he was transferred to palace attendant and presented the imperial seal to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，出爲宣城太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tianjian reign he went out as Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tianjian reign he went out as administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋入爲散騎常侍，領右驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the court as Palace Attendant and concurrently served as General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered court service as palace attendant and concurrently served as general of the right valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 六年，出爲平西始興王長史、南郡太守，父憂解職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went out as Chief Clerk on the staff of the Prince of Shixing of the Pacify-the-West command and Administrator of Nan Commandery, then left office upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he went out as chief clerk on the staff of the Prince of Shixing of the pacify-the-west command and as administrator of Nan commandery, then left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 居喪盡禮，廬于墓側，遺財悉推諸弟。

translations.literal: In mourning he observed every rite, built a hut beside the tomb, and gave all inherited property to his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he observed every rite, built a hut beside the tomb, and gave all inherited property to his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 八年，起爲持節、督司州諸軍事、信武將軍、司州刺史，領安陸太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Sizhou, General Who Gives Faith to Wu, and Regional Inspector of Sizhou, concurrently serving as Administrator of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Sizhou, general who gives faith to Wu, and regional inspector of Sizhou, concurrently serving as administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封豊城縣公。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 居州甚有威惠，爲邊人所悅服。

translations.literal: In his province he possessed great authority and kindness, and the frontier people were pleased to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he combined authority with kindness, and the frontier people were pleased to submit to him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以本號還朝，除都官尚書，遷給事中、右衛將軍、領豫州大中正。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he returned to court with his former title, was appointed Minister of Punishments, then transferred to Gentlemen Attendant, General of the Right Guard, and concurrently Grand Assessor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he returned to court with his former title, was appointed minister of punishments, then transferred to gentleman attendant, general of the right guard, and concurrently grand assessor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，出爲信武將軍、安西長史、江夏太守。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he went out as General Who Gives Faith to Wu, Chief Clerk on the Pacify-the-West staff, and Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he went out as general who gives faith to Wu, chief clerk on the pacify-the-west staff, and administrator of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入爲通直散騎常侍、太子右衛率，遷左衛將軍，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered court as Palace Attendant of Direct Communication and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then transferred to General of the Left Guard and concurrently General of the Vanguard Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he entered court as palace attendant of direct communication and left commandant of the crown prince's guard, then transferred to general of the left guard and concurrently general of the vanguard army.

sentences.zh: 俄出爲明威將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he went out as General of Illustrious Might and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he went out as general of illustrious might and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 在郡復有惠政，吏民圖其像，立碑頌美焉。

translations.literal: In the commandery he again carried out benevolent administration; officials and people painted his portrait and erected a stele in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he again carried out benevolent administration; officials and commoners painted his portrait and erected a stele in praise of him.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，入爲散騎常侍，領右驍騎將軍，轉太府卿，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Putong era he entered court as Palace Attendant, concurrently General of the Right Valiant Cavalry, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Treasury while retaining his post as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Putong era he entered court as palace attendant and concurrently general of the right valiant cavalry, then transferred to director of the imperial treasury while retaining his post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 以公事免，未幾，優詔復職。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an official matter, but before long a gracious edict restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an official matter, but before long a gracious edict restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷中護軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 六年，大舉北伐。

translations.literal: In the sixth year a great northern campaign was launched.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year a great northern campaign was launched.

sentences.zh: 先遣豫州刺史裴邃帥譙州刺史湛僧智、歷陽太守明紹世、南譙太守魚弘、晉熙太守張澄，並世之驍將，自南道伐壽陽城，未克而邃卒。

translations.literal: First the Regional Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Sui was sent leading the Regional Inspector of Qiao Zhan Sengzhi, Administrator of Liyang Ming Shaoshi, Administrator of Southern Qiao Yu Hong, and Administrator of Jinxi Zhang Cheng—all famed generals of the age—to attack Shouyang City by the southern route; before it was taken, Sui died.
translations.idiomatic: First Regional Inspector Pei Sui of Yuzhou was sent leading Regional Inspector Zhan Sengzhi of Qiao, Administrator Ming Shaoshi of Liyang, Administrator Yu Hong of Southern Qiao, and Administrator Zhang Cheng of Jinxi—all famed generals of the age—to attack Shouyang by the southern route; before the city fell, Sui died.

sentences.zh: 乃加亶使持節，馳驛代邃，與魏將河間王元琛、臨淮王元彧等相拒，頻戰克捷。

translations.literal: Dan was then given Bearer of the Staff, sent post-haste by relay to replace Sui, and opposed the Wei generals Prince Hejian Yuan Chen, Prince Linhuai Yuan Yu, and others, winning repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was then granted bearer of the staff and sent post-haste by relay to replace Sui; he opposed the Wei generals Prince Hejian Yuan Chen, Prince Linhuai Yuan Yu, and others, winning repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 尋有密敕，班師合肥，以休士馬，須堰成復進。

translations.literal: Soon there came a secret edict to withdraw the army to Hefei to rest men and horses, and to advance again once the dam was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a secret edict ordered the army to withdraw to Hefei to rest men and horses and to advance again once the dam was completed.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，淮堰水盛，壽陽城將沒，高祖復遣北道軍元樹帥彭寶孫、陳慶之等稍進，亶帥湛僧智、魚弘、張澄等通清流澗，將入淮、肥。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year the waters of the Huai dam swelled and Shouyang City was about to be submerged; the High Emperor again sent the northern-route army under Yuan Shu leading Peng Baosun, Chen Qingzhi, and others to advance gradually, while Dan led Zhan Sengzhi, Yu Hong, Zhang Cheng, and others through Qingliu Ravine, about to enter the Huai and Fei region.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the seventh year the waters of the Huai dam swelled and Shouyang was about to be submerged; Emperor Wu again sent the northern-route army under Yuan Shu, with Peng Baosun, Chen Qingzhi, and others, to advance gradually, while Dan led Zhan Sengzhi, Yu Hong, Zhang Cheng, and others through Qingliu Ravine toward the Huai and Fei region.

sentences.zh: 魏軍夾肥築城，出亶軍後，亶與僧智還襲，破之。

translations.literal: The Wei army built a city flanking the Fei and came out behind Dan's army; Dan and Sengzhi turned back and attacked, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army built a city flanking the Fei and came up behind Dan's army; Dan and Sengzhi turned back and attacked, defeating them.

sentences.zh: 進攻黎漿，貞威將軍韋放自北道會焉。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Lijiang, and General Who Proclaims Martial Faith Wei Fang joined them from the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to attack Lijiang, and General Who Proclaims Martial Faith Wei Fang joined them from the northern route.

sentences.zh: 兩軍既合，所向皆降下。

translations.literal: Once the two armies united, wherever they went cities surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two armies united, wherever they went cities surrendered.

sentences.zh: 凡降城五十二，獲男女口七萬五千人，米二十萬石。

translations.literal: In all fifty-two cities surrendered; they took seventy-five thousand men and women and two hundred thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In all fifty-two cities surrendered; they took seventy-five thousand men and women captive and two hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 詔以壽陽依前代置豫州，合肥鎮改爲南豫州，以亶爲使持節、都督豫州緣淮南豫霍義定五州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、豫、南豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict established Yuzhou at Shouyang according to former dynasties, changed the garrison at Hefei to Southern Yuzhou, and appointed Dan Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the five provinces of Yuzhou along the Huai, Huo, Yi, and Ding, General of the Cloud Banner, and Regional Inspector of both Yu and Southern Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established Yuzhou at Shouyang according to former dynasties, changed the garrison at Hefei to Southern Yuzhou, and appointed Dan bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs for the five provinces of Yuzhou along the Huai, Huo, Yi, and Ding, general of the cloud banner, and regional inspector of both Yu and Southern Yu provinces.

sentences.zh: 壽春久罹兵荒，百姓多流散，亶輕刑薄賦，務農省役，頃之民戶充復。

translations.literal: Shouchun had long suffered from war and desolation, and many common people had scattered; Dan lightened punishments and reduced taxes, devoted himself to agriculture and curtailed corvée labor, and before long the population was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun had long suffered from war and desolation, and many people had scattered; Dan lightened punishments and reduced taxes, devoted himself to agriculture and curtailed corvée labor, and before long the population was restored.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，進號平北將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Datong era his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Datong era he was promoted to general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒於州鎮。

translations.literal: In the third year he died at his provincial garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，卽日素服舉哀，贈車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor heard of it, that very day he wore plain garments and mourned; Dan was posthumously honored as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu heard of it, that very day he wore plain garments and mourned; Dan was posthumously honored as general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄。

translations.literal: His temple name was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 州民夏侯簡等五百人表請爲亶立碑置祠，詔許之。

translations.literal: Five hundred local people including Xiahou Jian submitted a petition requesting that a stele and shrine be erected for Dan, and the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred local people including Xiahou Jian submitted a petition requesting that a stele and shrine be erected for Dan, and the edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 亶爲人美風儀，寬厚有器量，涉獵文史，辯給能專對。

translations.literal: Dan was handsome in bearing, generous and possessed of capacity, widely read in literature and history, eloquent and able to respond aptly on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was handsome in bearing, generous and magnanimous, widely read in literature and history, and eloquent enough to hold his own in any exchange.

sentences.zh: 宗人夏侯溢爲衡陽內史，辭日，亶侍御坐，高祖謂亶曰：「夏侯溢於卿疏近？

translations.literal: His clansman Xiahou Yi served as Interior Minister of Hengyang; on the day of his farewell audience Dan attended at the imperial seat, and the High Emperor said to Dan, "Is Xiahou Yi closely related to you or distant?
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xiahou Yi served as interior minister of Hengyang; on the day of his farewell audience Dan attended at the imperial seat, and Emperor Wu said to Dan, "Is Xiahou Yi closely related to you or distant?

sentences.zh: 」稟答曰：「是臣從弟。

translations.literal: " Dan replied, "He is my younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: " Dan replied, "He is my younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 」高祖知溢于亶已疏，乃曰：「卿傖人，好不辨族從。

translations.literal: " The High Emperor knew that Yi was already distant from Dan in kinship, and said, "You rustic fellow—you cannot even distinguish your clan relations.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu knew that Yi was already distant from Dan in kinship, and said, "You rustic fellow—you cannot even distinguish your clan relations.

sentences.zh: 」亶對曰：「臣聞服屬易疏，所以不忍言族。

translations.literal: " Dan replied, "I have heard that with each degree of mourning obligation kin grows more distant; that is why I could not bear to speak of clan ties.
translations.idiomatic: " Dan replied, "I have heard that with each degree of mourning obligation kin grows more distant; that is why I could not bear to speak of clan ties.

sentences.zh: 」時以爲能對。

translations.literal: " At the time this was considered a skillful reply.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time this was considered a skillful reply.

sentences.zh: 亶歷爲六郡三州，不修產業，祿賜所得，隨散親故。

translations.literal: Dan served in six commanderies and three provinces, built up no estates, and distributed whatever salary and gifts he received among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Dan served in six commanderies and three provinces, built up no estates, and distributed whatever salary and gifts he received among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 性儉率，居處服用，充足而已，不事華侈。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and plain; in dwelling and dress he sought only sufficiency and did not pursue luxury.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and plain; in dwelling and dress he sought only sufficiency and did not pursue luxury.

sentences.zh: 晚年頗好音樂，有妓妾十數人，並無被服姿容。

translations.literal: In his later years he came to enjoy music greatly; he had a dozen or so singing girls and concubines, none of whom had fine clothing or beauty.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he came to enjoy music greatly; he had a dozen or so singing girls and concubines, none of whom had fine clothing or striking looks.

sentences.zh: 每有客，常隔簾奏之，時謂簾爲夏侯妓衣也。

translations.literal: Whenever he had guests, they would perform behind a curtain; at the time people called the curtain "the singing-girls' garment of the Xiahou clan."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had guests, they would perform behind a curtain; at the time people called the curtain "the singing-girls' garment of the Xiahou clan."

sentences.zh: 亶二子：誼，損。

translations.literal: Dan had two sons: Yi and Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had two sons: Yi and Sun.

sentences.zh: 誼襲封豊城公，歷官太子舍人，洗馬。

translations.literal: Yi inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fengcheng and held successive posts as Attendant of the Crown Prince and Groom.
translations.idiomatic: Yi inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Fengcheng and held successive posts as attendant of the crown prince and groom.

sentences.zh: 太清中，侯景入寇，誼與弟損帥部曲入城，並卒圍內。

translations.literal: During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing invaded, Yi and his younger brother Sun led their personal troops into the city and both died within the siege.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing invaded, Yi and his younger brother Sun led their personal troops into the city and both died within the siege.

sentences.zh: 八年，敕夔帥壯武將軍裴之禮、直閤將軍任思祖出義陽道，攻平靜、穆陵、陰山三關，克之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict ordered Kui to lead General of Martial Valor Pei Zhili and Colonel of the Palace Gateway Ren Sizu out by the Yiyang route to attack and take the three passes of Pingjing, Muling, and Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict ordered Kui to lead General of Martial Valor Pei Zhili and Colonel of the Palace Gateway Ren Sizu out by the Yiyang route to attack and take the three passes of Pingjing, Muling, and Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 是時譙州刺史湛僧智圍魏東豫州刺史元慶和於廣陵，入其郛。

translations.literal: At that time the Regional Inspector of Qiao Zhan Sengzhi besieged Yuan Qinghe, whom Wei had appointed Regional Inspector of Eastern Yu, at Guangling and entered the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Regional Inspector Zhan Sengzhi of Qiao besieged Yuan Qinghe, whom Wei had appointed regional inspector of Eastern Yu, at Guangling and entered the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 魏將元顯伯率軍赴援，僧智逆擊破之，夔自武陽會僧智，斷魏軍歸路。

translations.literal: The Wei general Yuan Xianbo led an army to relieve the siege; Sengzhi met and defeated him in a counterattack, and Kui joined Sengzhi from Wuyang, cutting off the Wei army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei general Yuan Xianbo led an army to relieve the siege; Sengzhi met and defeated him in a counterattack, and Kui joined Sengzhi from Wuyang, cutting off the Wei army's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 慶和於內築柵以自固，及夔至，遂請降。

translations.literal: Qinghe built palisades inside the city to hold firm; when Kui arrived, he asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe built palisades inside the city to hold firm; when Kui arrived, he asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 夔讓僧智，僧智曰：「慶和志欲降公，不願降僧智，今往必乖其意；

translations.literal: Kui yielded to Sengzhi, but Sengzhi said, "Qinghe wishes to surrender to you, sir, not to Sengzhi; if I go now I am sure to go against his intent;
translations.idiomatic: Kui yielded to Sengzhi, but Sengzhi said, "Qinghe wishes to surrender to you, sir, not to me; if I go now I am sure to go against his intent;

sentences.zh: 且僧智所將爲烏合募人，不可御之以法。

translations.literal: moreover, the troops I command are a rabble of recruited men and cannot be governed by strict law.
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the troops I command are a rabble of recruited men and cannot be governed by strict law.

sentences.zh: 公持軍素嚴，必無犯令，受降納附，深得其宜。

translations.literal: Your army has always been sternly disciplined and will surely not violate orders; receiving the surrender and accepting their submission is deeply fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your army has always been sternly disciplined and will surely not violate orders; receiving the surrender and accepting their submission is deeply fitting.

sentences.zh: 」於是夔乃登城拔魏幟，建官軍旗鼓，衆莫敢妄動，慶和束兵以出，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Kui ascended the wall, pulled down the Wei banners, and raised the banners and drums of the imperial army; none dared stir rashly; Qinghe bound his troops and came out, and the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Kui ascended the wall, pulled down the Wei banners, and raised the banners and drums of the imperial army; none dared stir rashly; Qinghe bound his troops and came out, and the army took nothing for private gain.

sentences.zh: 凡降男女口四萬餘人，粟六十萬斛，餘物稱是。

translations.literal: In all more than forty thousand men and women surrendered, along with six hundred thousand piculs of grain and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: In all more than forty thousand men and women surrendered, along with six hundred thousand piculs of grain and other goods in proportion.

sentences.zh: 顯伯聞之夜遁，衆軍追之，生擒二萬餘人，斬獲不可勝數。

translations.literal: Xianbo heard of it and fled by night; the armies pursued him, took more than twenty thousand alive, and the slain and captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbo heard of it and fled by night; the armies pursued him, took more than twenty thousand alive, and the slain and captured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 詔以僧智領東豫州，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Sengzhi to oversee Eastern Yuzhou and garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Sengzhi to oversee Eastern Yuzhou and garrison Guangling.

sentences.zh: 夔引軍屯安陽。

translations.literal: Kui led his army to encamp at Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui led his army to encamp at Anyang.

sentences.zh: 夔又遣偏將屠楚城，盡俘其衆，由是義陽北道遂與魏絕。

translations.literal: Kui also sent a subordinate general to storm Chu City, capturing its entire force; thereby the northern route of Yiyang was cut off from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Kui also sent a subordinate general to storm Chu City and capture its entire force; thereby the northern route of Yiyang was cut off from Wei.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，魏郢州刺史元願達請降，高祖敕郢州刺史元樹往迎願達，夔亦自楚城會之，遂留鎮焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Datong era, Yuan Yuanda, whom Wei had appointed Regional Inspector of Ying, asked to surrender; the High Emperor ordered the Regional Inspector of Ying Yuan Shu to go welcome Yuanda, and Kui also joined him from Chu City and remained to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Datong era, Yuan Yuanda, whom Wei had appointed regional inspector of Ying, asked to surrender; Emperor Wu ordered Regional Inspector Yuan Shu of Ying to go welcome him, and Kui also joined him from Chu City and remained to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 詔改魏郢州爲北司州，以夔爲刺史，兼督司州。

translations.literal: An edict changed Wei's Ying Province to Northern Sizhou and appointed Kui as its regional inspector, concurrently supervising Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict changed Wei's Ying province to Northern Sizhou and appointed Kui as its regional inspector, concurrently supervising Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷使持節，進號仁威將軍，封保城縣侯，邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, his title advanced to General of Humane Might, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made bearer of the staff, promoted to general of humane might, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Baocheng with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，徵爲右衛將軍，丁所生母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhongdatong era he was summoned as General of the Right Guard and left office upon the death of his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhongdatong era he was summoned as general of the right guard and left office upon the death of his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 時魏南兗州刺史劉明以譙城入附，詔遣鎮北將軍元樹帥軍應接，起夔爲雲麾將軍，隨機北討。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ming, whom Wei had appointed Regional Inspector of Southern Yan, surrendered Qiao City to the Liang; an edict sent General Who Guards the North Yuan Shu with an army to support him, and Kui was recalled as General of the Cloud Banner to join the northern campaign as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Ming, whom Wei had appointed regional inspector of Southern Yan, surrendered Qiao City to the Liang; an edict sent General Who Guards the North Yuan Shu with an army to support him, and Kui was recalled as general of the cloud banner to join the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Bearer of the Staff, made Supervisor of Military Affairs in Southern Yuzhou, and appointed Regional Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted bearer of the staff, made supervisor of military affairs in Southern Yuzhou, and appointed regional inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉使持節、督豫淮陳潁建霍義七州諸軍事、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the seven provinces of Yu, Huai, Chen, Ying, Jian, Huo, and Yi, and Regional Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the seven provinces of Yu, Huai, Chen, Ying, Jian, Huo, and Yi, and regional inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫州積歲寇戎，人頗失業，夔乃帥軍人于蒼陵立堰，溉田千餘頃。

translations.literal: Yuzhou had suffered raids and warfare for years and many people had lost their livelihoods; Kui therefore led his soldiers to build a dam at Cangling and irrigate more than a thousand acres of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou had suffered raids and warfare for years and many people had lost their livelihoods; Kui therefore led his soldiers to build a dam at Cangling and irrigate more than a thousand acres of fields.

sentences.zh: 歲收穀百餘萬石，以充儲備，兼贍貧人，境內賴之。

translations.literal: Each year the harvest exceeded a million piculs of grain, which filled the stores, supported the poor as well, and the whole region relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the harvest exceeded a million piculs of grain, which filled the stores, supported the poor as well, and the whole region relied on it.

sentences.zh: 夔兄亶先經此任，至是夔又居焉。

translations.literal: Kui's elder brother Dan had previously held this post; now Kui held it in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's elder brother Dan had previously held this post; now Kui held it in turn.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並有恩惠於鄉里，百姓歌之曰：「我之有州，頻仍夏侯；

translations.literal: Both brothers had shown kindness to the region, and the people sang of them: "That we have this province is thanks again and again to the Xiahou clan;
translations.idiomatic: Both brothers had shown kindness to the region, and the people sang of them: "That we have this province is thanks again and again to the Xiahou clan;

sentences.zh: 前兄後弟，布政優優。

translations.literal: the elder brother first, the younger brother after—their governance is gentle and good."
translations.idiomatic: the elder brother first, the younger brother after—their governance is gentle and good."

sentences.zh: 」在州七年，甚有聲績，遠近多附之。

translations.literal: He was in the province seven years and won great renown and achievement; many from near and far attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was in the province seven years and won great renown and achievement; many from near and far attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 有部曲萬人，馬二千匹，並服習精強，爲當時之盛。

translations.literal: He had ten thousand personal troops and two thousand horses, all well trained and formidable—the greatest force of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten thousand personal troops and two thousand horses, all well trained and formidable—the greatest force of the age.

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，後房伎妾曳羅縠飾金翠者亦有百數。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and proud; in his inner quarters he had a hundred or so singing girls and concubines trailing gauze robes adorned with gold and kingfisher feathers.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant and proud; in his inner quarters he had a hundred or so singing girls and concubines in trailing gauze robes adorned with gold and kingfisher feathers.

sentences.zh: 愛好人士，不以貴勢自高，文武賓客常滿坐，時亦以此稱之。

translations.literal: He loved and honored men of talent, did not hold himself high because of rank and power, and his civil and military guests constantly filled his seats; at the time he was praised for this as well.
translations.idiomatic: He loved and honored men of talent, did not hold himself high because of rank and power, and his civil and military guests constantly filled his hall; at the time he was praised for this as well.

sentences.zh: 大同四年，卒于州，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Datong era he died in the province at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Datong era he died in the province at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 有詔舉哀，賻錢二十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered mourning; condolence money of two hundred thousand and two hundred bolts of cloth were granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered mourning; condolence money of two hundred thousand and two hundred bolts of cloth were granted.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、安北將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as palace attendant and general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 諡曰桓。

translations.literal: His temple name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Huan.

sentences.zh: 子撰嗣，官至太僕卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhuan succeeded him and rose to Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuan succeeded him and rose to director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 撰弟譒，少粗險薄行，常停鄉里，領其父部曲，爲州助防，刺史蕭淵明引爲府長史。

translations.literal: Zhuan's younger brother Bo was coarse and treacherous in youth, with base conduct; he often remained in his home district, commanded his father's personal troops, served as the province's assistant defense commander, and was brought in by Regional Inspector Xiao Yuanming as chief clerk of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan's younger brother Bo was coarse and treacherous in youth, with base conduct; he often remained in his home district, commanded his father's personal troops, served as the province's assistant defense commander, and was recruited by Regional Inspector Xiao Yuanming as chief clerk of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 淵明彭城戰沒，復爲侯景長史。

translations.literal: When Yuanming fell in battle at Pengcheng, Bo again served as chief clerk to Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanming fell in battle at Pengcheng, Bo again served as chief clerk to Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景尋舉兵反，譒前驅濟江，頓兵城西士林館，破掠邸第及居人富室，子女財貨，盡略有之。

translations.literal: When Jing soon raised his army in rebellion, Bo served as vanguard crossing the Yangtze, encamped his troops at the Shilin Lodge west of the city, and stormed and plundered mansions and the homes of wealthy residents, seizing all their sons and daughters, goods, and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing soon raised his army in rebellion, Bo served as vanguard crossing the Yangtze, encamped at the Shilin Lodge west of the city, and stormed and plundered mansions and the homes of the wealthy, seizing their sons and daughters, goods, and wealth.

sentences.zh: 淵明在州有四妾，章、於、王、阮，並有國色。

translations.literal: Yuanming had four concubines in the province—Zhang, Yu, Wang, and Ruan—all of national beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming had four concubines in the province—Zhang, Yu, Wang, and Ruan—all renowned for their beauty.

sentences.zh: 淵明沒魏，其妾並還京第，譒至，破第納焉。

translations.literal: When Yuanming died in Wei territory, his concubines all returned to his capital mansion; when Bo arrived, he broke into the mansion and took them in.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanming died in Wei territory, his concubines all returned to his capital mansion; when Bo arrived, he broke into the mansion and took them for himself.

sentences.zh: 魚弘，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Yu Hong was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hong came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，白皙美姿容。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with fair skin and handsome features.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with fair skin and handsome features.

sentences.zh: 累從征討，常爲軍鋒，歷南譙、盱眙、竟陵太守。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns, often served as the army's spearhead, and held successive posts as Administrator of Southern Qiao, Xuyi, and Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly followed campaigns, often served as the army's spearhead, and held successive posts as administrator of Southern Qiao, Xuyi, and Jingling.

sentences.zh: 常語人曰：「我爲郡，所謂四盡：水中魚鱉盡，山中麞鹿盡，田中米穀盡，村里民庶盡。

translations.literal: He often told people, "When I govern a commandery, it is what is called the four exhaustions: fish and turtles in the water exhausted, deer and roe in the mountains exhausted, grain in the fields exhausted, and common people in the villages exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "When I govern a commandery, it is what people call the four exhaustions: the fish and turtles in the water are exhausted, the deer in the mountains are exhausted, the grain in the fields is exhausted, and the common people in the villages are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 丈夫生世，如輕塵栖弱草，白駒之過隙。

translations.literal: A man's life in this world is like light dust settling on fragile grass, or a white colt flashing past a crack.
translations.idiomatic: A man's life in this world is like light dust on fragile grass, or a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.

sentences.zh: 人生歡樂富貴幾何時！

translations.literal: How long do joy, wealth, and honor in human life last!
translations.idiomatic: How long do joy, wealth, and honor in human life last!

sentences.zh: 」於是恣意酣賞，侍妾百餘人，不勝金翠，服玩車馬，皆窮一時之絕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he indulged himself in unrestrained revelry; he had more than a hundred serving girls and concubines laden with gold and kingfisher ornaments, and his clothing, curios, chariots, and horses were all the utmost extravagance of the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he indulged himself in unrestrained revelry; he had more than a hundred serving girls and concubines laden with gold and kingfisher ornaments, and his clothing, curios, chariots, and horses were all the utmost extravagance of the age.

sentences.zh: 遷爲平西湘東王司馬、新興、永寧二郡太守，卒官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Marshal on the Pacify-the-West staff of the Prince of Xiangdong and Administrator of the two commanderies of Xinxing and Yongning, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to marshal on the pacify-the-west staff of the Prince of Xiangdong and administrator of the two commanderies of Xinxing and Yongning, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 六年，大舉北伐，以放爲貞威將軍，與胡龍牙會曹仲宗進軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, during the great northern campaign, Fang was made General Who Proclaims Martial Faith and joined Hu Longya in meeting Cao Zhongzong to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, during the great northern campaign, Fang was made general who proclaims martial faith and joined Hu Longya in meeting Cao Zhongzong to advance the army.

sentences.zh: 七年，夏侯亶攻黎漿不克，高祖復使帥軍自北道會壽春城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Xiahou Dan failed to take Lijiang, the High Emperor again sent him to lead an army from the northern route to join forces at Shouchun City.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Xiahou Dan failed to take Lijiang, Emperor Wu again sent him to lead an army from the northern route to join forces at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雲麾南康王長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Cloud-Banner staff of the Prince of Nankang and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to chief clerk on the cloud-banner staff of the Prince of Nankang and administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 放累爲籓佐，並著聲績。

translations.literal: Fang repeatedly served as a prince's staff officer and distinguished himself in reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Fang repeatedly served as a prince's staff officer and distinguished himself in reputation and achievement.

sentences.zh: 普通八年，高祖遣兼領軍曹仲宗等攻渦陽，又以放爲明威將軍，帥師會之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Putong era, the High Emperor sent the Acting Commander of the Army Cao Zhongzong and others to attack Woyang, and again appointed Fang General of Illustrious Might to lead troops and join them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Putong era, Emperor Wu sent Acting Commander of the Army Cao Zhongzong and others to attack Woyang, and again appointed Fang general of illustrious might to lead troops and join them.

sentences.zh: 魏大將費穆帥衆奄至，放軍營未立，麾下止有二百餘人。

translations.literal: The Wei grand general Fei Mu led his troops in a sudden arrival; Fang's camp was not yet established, and he had only a little more than two hundred men under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei grand general Fei Mu led his troops in a sudden arrival; Fang's camp was not yet established, and he had only a little more than two hundred men under his command.

sentences.zh: 放從弟洵驍果有勇力，一軍所仗，放令洵單騎擊刺，屢折魏軍，洵馬亦被傷不能進，放胄又三貫流矢。

translations.literal: Fang's younger cousin Xun was valiant and possessed strength and courage, the man the whole army relied on; Fang ordered Xun to charge alone on horseback and strike repeatedly, breaking the Wei army again and again; Xun's horse was also wounded and could not advance, and three stray arrows pierced Fang's helmet.
