translations.idiomatic: Fang's younger cousin Xun was valiant and possessed strength and courage, the man the whole army relied on; Fang ordered Xun to charge alone on horseback and strike repeatedly, breaking the Wei army again and again; Xun's horse was also wounded and could not advance, and three stray arrows pierced Fang's helmet.

sentences.zh: 衆皆失色，請放突去。

translations.literal: All turned pale and begged Fang to break out and flee.
translations.idiomatic: All turned pale and begged Fang to break out and flee.

sentences.zh: 放厲聲叱之曰：「今日唯有死耳。

translations.literal: Fang shouted sternly at them, "Today there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: Fang shouted sternly at them, "Today there is only death.

sentences.zh: 」乃免胄下馬，據胡床處分。

translations.literal: " He then removed his helmet, dismounted, and sat on a folding camp chair to give orders.
translations.idiomatic: " He then removed his helmet, dismounted, and sat on a folding camp chair to give orders.

sentences.zh: 於是士皆殊死戰，莫不一當百。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers all fought as if facing death, each man matching a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the soldiers all fought as if facing death, each man matching a hundred.

sentences.zh: 魏軍遂退，放逐北至渦陽。

translations.literal: The Wei army then withdrew, and Fang pursued them north to Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army then withdrew, and Fang pursued them north to Woyang.

sentences.zh: 魏又遣常山王元昭、大將軍李獎、乞佛寶、費穆等衆五萬來援，放率所督將陳度、趙伯超等夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Wei again sent Prince Changshan Yuan Zhao, the great general Li Jiang, Qifo Bao, Fei Mu, and others with fifty thousand troops as reinforcements; Fang led the generals under his command, Chen Du and Zhao Bochao, in a pincer attack and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again sent Prince Changshan Yuan Zhao, the great general Li Jiang, Qifo Bao, Fei Mu, and others with fifty thousand troops as reinforcements; Fang led the generals under his command, Chen Du and Zhao Bochao, in a pincer attack and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 渦陽城主王緯以城降。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, the lord of Woyang City, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, the lord of Woyang, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 放乃登城，簡出降口四千二百人，器仗充牣；

translations.literal: Fang then ascended the wall, selected and released four thousand two hundred surrendered people, and the weapons and armor were fully stocked;
translations.idiomatic: Fang then ascended the wall, selected and released four thousand two hundred surrendered people, and the weapons and armor were fully stocked;

sentences.zh: 又遣降人三十，分報李獎、費穆等。

translations.literal: he also sent thirty surrendered men to report separately to Li Jiang, Fei Mu, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent thirty surrendered men to report separately to Li Jiang, Fei Mu, and the others.

sentences.zh: 魏人棄諸營壘，一時奔潰，衆軍乘之，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: The Wei men abandoned all their camps and fortifications and fled in rout at once; the armies pursued them and slaughtered and captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops abandoned all their camps and fortifications and fled in rout at once; the armies pursued them and slaughtered and captured nearly all.

sentences.zh: 擒穆弟超，並王緯送於京師。

translations.literal: They captured Mu's younger brother Chao, and together with Wang Wei sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Mu's younger brother Chao and, together with Wang Wei, sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 還爲太子右衛率，轉通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, then transferred to Palace Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made right commandant of the crown prince's guard, then transferred to palace attendant of direct communication.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督梁南秦二州諸軍事、信武將軍、梁南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Liang and Southern Qin, General Who Gives Faith to Wu, and Regional Inspector of both Liang and Southern Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Liang and Southern Qin, general who gives faith to Wu, and regional inspector of both Liang and Southern Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，徙督北徐州諸軍事、北徐州刺史，增封四百戶，持節、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhongdatong era he was transferred to Supervisor of Military Affairs in Northern Xuzhou and Regional Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, his fief increased by four hundred households, with Bearer of the Staff and his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhongdatong era he was transferred to supervisor of military affairs in Northern Xuzhou and regional inspector of Northern Xuzhou, his fief increased by four hundred households, with bearer of the staff and his general's title unchanged.

sentences.zh: 在鎮三年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: He was at his garrison three years and died at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was at his garrison three years and died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宜侯。

translations.literal: His temple name was Yihou.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Yihou.

sentences.zh: 放性弘厚篤實，輕財好施，于諸弟尤雍睦。

translations.literal: Fang was generous, sincere, and solid in character, light with wealth and fond of giving, and especially harmonious with his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was generous, sincere, and solid in character, light with wealth and fond of giving, and especially harmonious with his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 每將遠別及行役初還，常同一室臥起，時稱爲「三姜」。

translations.literal: Whenever he was about to part on a distant journey or had just returned from service on campaign, they would sleep and rise in the same room; at the time they were called "the three Jiang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was about to part on a distant journey or had just returned from service on campaign, they would sleep and rise in the same room; at the time they were called "the three Jiang brothers."

sentences.zh: 初，放與吳郡張率皆有側室懷孕，因指爲婚姻。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fang and Zhang Shuai of Wu Commandery both had concubines who were pregnant, and they therefore pledged their children in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fang and Zhang Shuai of Wu commandery both had concubines who were pregnant, and they therefore pledged their children in marriage.

sentences.zh: 其後各產男女，未及成長而率亡，遺嗣孤弱，放常贍卹之。

translations.literal: Later each had sons and daughters, but before they reached maturity Shuai died, leaving orphaned heirs weak and helpless; Fang constantly supported and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Later each had sons and daughters, but before they reached maturity Shuai died, leaving orphaned heirs weak and helpless; Fang constantly supported and comforted them.

sentences.zh: 及爲北徐州，時有勢族請姻者，放曰：「吾不失信於故友。

translations.literal: When he became Regional Inspector of Northern Xuzhou, a powerful clan sought a marriage alliance; Fang said, "I will not break faith with an old friend.
translations.idiomatic: When he became regional inspector of Northern Xuzhou, a powerful clan sought a marriage alliance; Fang said, "I will not break faith with an old friend.

sentences.zh: 」乃以息岐娶率女，又以女適率子，時稱放能篤舊。

translations.literal: " He therefore had his son Qi marry Shuai's daughter and gave his own daughter to Shuai's son; at the time Fang was praised for his loyalty to old ties.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore had his son Qi marry Shuai's daughter and gave his own daughter to Shuai's son; at the time Fang was praised for his loyalty to old ties.

sentences.zh: 長子粲嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Can succeeded him; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Can succeeded him; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：裴邃之詞采早著，兼思略沉深，夏侯稟之好學辯給，夔之奢豪愛士，韋放之弘厚篤行，並遇主逢時，展其才用矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Pei Sui's literary brilliance showed early, and he combined deep strategic thought; Xiahou Dan loved learning and was eloquent; Kui was extravagant yet loved men of talent; Wei Fang was generous, sincere, and solid in conduct—all met their ruler and seized the moment to display their talents.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Pei Sui's literary brilliance showed early, and he combined deep strategic thought; Xiahou Dan loved learning and was eloquent; Kui was extravagant yet loved men of talent; Wei Fang was generous, sincere, and solid in conduct—all met their ruler and seized the moment to display their talents.

sentences.zh: 及牧州典郡，破敵安邊，咸著功績，允文武之任，蓋梁室之名臣歟。

translations.literal: When they governed provinces and administered commanderies, defeated enemies and secured the frontier, all achieved notable merit and were fit for civil and military duties—were they not famed ministers of the Liang house?
translations.idiomatic: When they governed provinces and administered commanderies, defeated enemies and secured the frontier, all achieved notable merit and were fit for civil and military duties—were they not famed ministers of the Liang house?
